> **Discussion points.** (1) Within a small window, correlations close to ±1 are common by chance, so the map needs a significance test or a larger window before it is interpreted. (2) The predictions do not include effort, which is right for this question, but they include the spatial random fields, so part of the overlap may come from where hauls were taken. (3) Simpler, whole-area summaries of overlap would complement the map: for example, the share of trawling hours in the cells with the highest predicted biomass, or a per-cell correlation across the eight years. (4) The axis labels read "UTM 33N" but the coordinates are in degrees.

> **Still to share:** the script behind the correlation map (variables, window, method).

### 2c.10 Marine heatwaves, biomass trends and trawling trends

The group's last step relates the red mullet model to marine heatwaves (MHWs) and to trawling. For each grid cell of the predictions, it combines three layers: summer heatwave exposure, the 2014-2021 linear trend in predicted biomass, and the 2014-2021 linear trend in trawling hours. The trends were computed by the group (`df_slope_6.rds`, `df_slope.rds`); they match exactly a per-cell linear regression of the predicted biomass (`pred_*.rds`) and of the yearly trawling hours (`eff_grid_*.rds`) on year.

The heatwave metrics are recomputed here for both areas on the prediction grid, with the method of Section 3 (Hobday et al. 2016, `heatwaveR`, summer events peaking in June-August). The group's two scripts are included in the repository with relative paths (`scripts/5_MHW_grids.R`, adapted from `mhw_GSA6.R`; `scripts/6_MHW_trend_maps.R`, adapted from `Plot_MHW_BiologicalTrend_Effor_ttrend.R`).

```{r grp-mhw-run}
#| eval: false
#| code-summary: "Compute heatwave metrics on both prediction grids (not evaluated: needs the daily SST NetCDF)"

source("scripts/5_MHW_grids.R")   # writes outputs/MHW_grid_6.csv and outputs/MHW_grid_1718.csv
```

```{r grp-mhw-load}
#| code-summary: "Load the heatwave metrics and compare with the group's Adriatic file"
#| cache: false

mhw_g <- bind_rows(read.csv("outputs/MHW_grid_6.csv") |> mutate(region = "GSA 6"),
                   read.csv("outputs/MHW_grid_1718.csv") |> mutate(region = "GSAs 17-18"))

# Check against the group's Adriatic metrics (MHW_gsa17.csv), cell by cell
mhw_chk <- read.csv("outputs/MHW_grid_1718.csv") |>
  mutate(X = round(X, 4), Y = round(Y, 4)) |>
  inner_join(read.csv("data/group/MHW_gsa17.csv", sep = ";") |>
               transmute(X = round(X, 4), Y = round(Y, 4), YEAR, group_cum = mhw_cum_intensity),
             by = c("X", "Y", "YEAR"))
mhw_same <- with(filter(mhw_chk, sst_available), mean(abs(mhw_cum_intensity - group_cum) < 1e-6))
mhw_nosst <- with(filter(mhw_chk, !sst_available), sum(YEAR == 2014))

mhw_year <- mhw_g |>
  group_by(region, YEAR) |>
  summarise(cum = mean(mhw_cum_intensity, na.rm = TRUE), days = mean(mhw_days, na.rm = TRUE),
            .groups = "drop")
```

For the Adriatic, the recomputed metrics are identical to the group's file (`MHW_gsa17.csv`) in `r percent(mhw_same, 0.1)` of cell-years with SST data. The difference is in `r mhw_nosst` cells (`r percent(mhw_nosst / n_distinct(mhw_chk$X, mhw_chk$Y), 1)` of the grid), almost all north of 45.0°N, where the SST product has no data: the group's file gives them zero heatwaves, while here they are left missing.

```{r fig-grp-mhw-years}
#| fig-cap: "Mean summer cumulative heatwave intensity per year across each area's prediction grid (°C days). Points mark the three strongest and three weakest summers from 2015 onward, after the AIS ramp-up, proposed as contrasting years for each area."
#| fig-width: 9
#| fig-height: 4.2

mhw_pick <- mhw_year |>
  filter(YEAR >= 2015) |>
  group_by(region) |>
  mutate(rank = rank(-cum, ties.method = "first"),
         class = case_when(rank <= 3 ~ "Strong MHW summer", rank >= n() - 2 ~ "Weak MHW summer")) |>
  ungroup() |> filter(!is.na(class))

ggplot(mhw_year, aes(YEAR, cum, colour = region)) +
  annotate("rect", xmin = 2011.6, xmax = 2014.5, ymin = -Inf, ymax = Inf, fill = "grey92") +
  annotate("text", x = 2013, y = max(mhw_year$cum), label = "AIS ramp-up", colour = "grey45", size = 3.2) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.9) +
  geom_point(data = mhw_pick, aes(shape = class), size = 3) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = grp_cols, name = NULL) +
  scale_shape_manual(values = c(`Strong MHW summer` = 16, `Weak MHW summer` = 1), name = NULL) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = 2012:2021) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Cumulative intensity (°C days)") + theme_ocean()
```

```{r tbl-grp-mhw-years}
#| tbl-cap: "Proposed contrasting summers for each area, from 2015 onward. Area: GSA 6 or GSAs 17-18. Strong MHW summers, Weak MHW summers: the three years with the highest and lowest mean summer cumulative heatwave intensity across the area's prediction grid (in brackets, °C days). The GSA 6 comparison in Section 3.2 uses 2017, 2018, 2020 against 2013, 2014, 2016."
#| classes: tbl-compact

kable(mhw_pick |>
        mutate(lab = sprintf("%d (%.1f)", YEAR, cum)) |>
        arrange(region, class, YEAR) |>
        group_by(Area = region, class) |>
        summarise(years = paste(lab, collapse = ", "), .groups = "drop") |>
        pivot_wider(names_from = class, values_from = years))
```

The two areas do not share their heatwave years. In GSA 6, the strongest summers are `r paste(sort(mhw_pick$YEAR[mhw_pick$region == "GSA 6" & mhw_pick$class == "Strong MHW summer"]), collapse = ", ")`; in the Adriatic, `r paste(sort(mhw_pick$YEAR[mhw_pick$region == "GSAs 17-18" & mhw_pick$class == "Strong MHW summer"]), collapse = ", ")`, while 2020, a strong year in GSA 6, had almost no heatwave in the Adriatic. Any comparison between heatwave and non-heatwave years therefore needs area-specific years.

```{r grp-trends}
#| code-summary: "Heatwave, biomass trend and trawling trend maps (scripts/6_MHW_trend_maps.R)"
#| cache: false

source("scripts/6_MHW_trend_maps.R")
trend_g <- bind_rows(trend_data("6") |> mutate(region = "GSA 6"),
                     trend_data("1718") |> mutate(region = "GSAs 17-18"))
```

```{r fig-grp-trends-6}
#| fig-cap: "GSA 6. A: mean summer cumulative heatwave intensity, 2014-2021 (°C days per summer). B: linear trend in predicted red mullet biomass, 2014-2021, as a percentage of the cell's mean biomass per year. C: linear trend in trawling hours, 2014-2021, as a percentage of the cell's mean hours per year (grey: less than 1 hour per year on average). Trend colour scales are capped at ±15% per year."
#| fig-width: 10
#| fig-height: 5.6

trend_maps("6", filter(trend_g, region == "GSA 6"))
```

```{r fig-grp-trends-1718}
#| fig-cap: "GSAs 17-18 (Adriatic). Panels as in the GSA 6 figure. Grey in A: no SST data (north of 45.0°N)."
#| fig-width: 12
#| fig-height: 5.2

trend_maps("1718", filter(trend_g, region == "GSAs 17-18"))
```

```{r tbl-grp-trends}
#| tbl-cap: "Summary of the heatwave and trend layers by area. Area: GSA 6 or GSAs 17-18. MHW intensity (°C days per summer): median over cells of the 2014-2021 mean summer cumulative heatwave intensity. Biomass trend (%/yr), Trawling trend (%/yr): median over cells of the linear trend, as a percentage of the cell's mean per year. Cells with biomass decline, Cells with trawling decline: share of cells with a negative trend. r (MHW, biomass trend), r (MHW, trawling trend): Spearman correlation across cells between heatwave intensity and each trend."
#| classes: tbl-compact

kable(trend_g |>
        group_by(Area = region) |>
        summarise(`MHW intensity (°C days per summer)` = round(median(mhw_cum, na.rm = TRUE), 1),
                  `Biomass trend (%/yr)` = round(median(trend_bio), 1),
                  `Cells with biomass decline` = percent(mean(trend_bio < 0), 1),
                  `Trawling trend (%/yr)` = round(median(trend_eff, na.rm = TRUE), 1),
                  `Cells with trawling decline` = percent(mean(trend_eff < 0, na.rm = TRUE), 1),
                  `r (MHW, biomass trend)` = round(cor(mhw_cum, trend_bio, method = "spearman", use = "complete.obs"), 2),
                  `r (MHW, trawling trend)` = round(cor(mhw_cum, trend_eff, method = "spearman", use = "complete.obs"), 2)))
```

Trends are shown relative to each cell's mean, so that biomass (kg/km²) and effort (hours) are on the same scale and one threshold means the same for both. In GSA 6, predicted biomass rises slightly over most of the shelf, while trawling trends form a fine mosaic of increases and decreases. In the Adriatic, biomass trends follow the broad patches of the spatio-temporal field, and heatwave exposure is highest along the Italian coast and in the south.

> **Discussion points.** (1) The heatwave map in the group's script grouped the data by year and cell, so the ten yearly maps were drawn on top of each other and only the last year was visible; here the panel shows the mean summer cumulative intensity over 2014-2021, the period of the trends. (2) The group classed trends as decreasing, stable or increasing with a threshold of ±0.1 in absolute units (kg/km² per year for biomass, hours per year for effort), which leaves only about 3% of cells "stable" in the Adriatic; relative trends, as here, or classes based on significance are more meaningful. Significance of the slopes is to be shared by the group and can then be used to grey out non-significant trends. (3) The biomass trends come from model predictions that include the spatio-temporal field, so in the Adriatic part of the pattern reflects year-to-year noise in that field. (4) The climatology uses 2010-2021, shorter than the 30-year baseline recommended by Hobday et al. (2016).

### 2c.11 Trawling in strong and weak heatwave summers

Section 3.2 compares trawling in GSA 6 between heatwave summers (2017, 2018, 2020) and quieter ones (2013, 2014, 2016), and the group had started to redo this on the new grid (`mhw_GSA6.R`). Here the comparison is made for both areas with each area's own contrasting summers (@tbl-grp-mhw-years), all from 2015 onward so that the AIS ramp-up does not enter the contrast. Daily trawler effort for June-August is downloaded at 0.01° with `gfwr`, and each summer is summarised by fleet-level metrics (`scripts/7_fleet_MHW.R`).

```{r grp-fleet-run}
#| eval: false
#| code-summary: "Download summer trawler effort and summarise it (not evaluated: calls the GFW API)"

source("scripts/7_fleet_MHW.R")   # writes outputs/fleet_MHW_*.csv
```

```{r grp-fleet-load}
#| code-summary: "Load the fleet summaries"
#| cache: false

fleet_s <- read.csv("outputs/fleet_MHW_summary.csv") |>
  mutate(class = factor(class, c("weak", "strong"), c("Weak MHW summer", "Strong MHW summer")))
fleet_c <- read.csv("outputs/fleet_MHW_cells.csv")
```

```{r fig-grp-fleet}
#| cache: false
#| fig-cap: "Fleet metrics for each summer (June-August), trawlers only, as the percentage difference from the area's mean over the six summers. Filled points: strong heatwave summers; open points: weak ones; bars: mean of each group. Shelf share: share of trawling hours at depths of 200 m or less, where red mullet lives. Absolute values are in the table below."
#| fig-width: 11
#| fig-height: 4.6

fleet_long <- fleet_s |>
  transmute(region, year, class,
            `Total hours (thousands)` = total_hours / 1000, `Active vessels` = vessels,
            `Hours per vessel` = hours_per_vessel, `Mean depth (m)` = mean_depth_m,
            `Mean distance to coast (km)` = mean_dist_coast_km, `Shelf share (%)` = 100 * shelf_share) |>
  pivot_longer(-c(region, year, class)) |>
  mutate(name = factor(name, unique(name))) |>
  group_by(region, name) |> mutate(rel = 100 * (value / mean(value) - 1)) |> ungroup()
fleet_mean <- fleet_long |> group_by(region, class, name) |> summarise(rel = mean(rel), .groups = "drop")
dodge <- position_dodge(width = 0.6)

ggplot(fleet_long, aes(region, rel, colour = region, group = class)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, colour = "grey70") +
  geom_crossbar(data = fleet_mean, aes(ymin = rel, ymax = rel), width = 0.25, linewidth = 0.4, position = dodge) +
  geom_point(aes(shape = class), size = 2.3, position = dodge) +
  scale_shape_manual(values = c(`Weak MHW summer` = 1, `Strong MHW summer` = 16), name = NULL) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = grp_cols, guide = "none") +
  scale_x_discrete(labels = c(`GSA 6` = "GSA 6", `GSAs 17-18` = "17-18")) +
  facet_wrap(~name, nrow = 1, labeller = label_wrap_gen(14)) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Difference from the six-summer mean (%)") + theme_ocean(10)
```

There is no consistent difference in fleet behaviour between strong and weak heatwave summers in either area. Total trawling hours differ by `r fleet_tab2$Difference[fleet_tab2$Area == "GSA 6" & fleet_tab2$Metric == "Total hours (thousands)"]` in GSA 6 and `r fleet_tab2$Difference[fleet_tab2$Area == "GSAs 17-18" & fleet_tab2$Metric == "Total hours (thousands)"]` in the Adriatic, well within the spread between individual summers, and the number of vessels, the depth and distance to coast of fishing and the share of effort on the shelf barely change. The cell map shows a mosaic of local increases and decreases rather than a coherent shift. This contrasts with Section 3.2, where effort appeared higher in heatwave years: with the early, low-AIS years removed from the contrast, that difference disappears.

#### 2c.11.1 Do strong and weak heatwave summers use the same fishing grounds?

Similar totals could hide a move to other grounds. Three spatial measures test this on the 0.05° grid, for each pair of summers:

- **Distribution overlap (Schoener's D):** D = 1 − ½ Σ |pᵢ − qᵢ|, where pᵢ and qᵢ are the shares of a summer's trawling hours in cell i. D = 1 when effort is spread identically over the cells, 0 when the two summers share no cell.
- **Core grounds:** for each summer, the smallest set of cells holding 80% of its trawling hours. Their overlap between two summers is measured with the Jaccard index (cells core in both / cells core in either).
- **Centre of gravity:** the effort-weighted mean position of trawling in each summer.

If heatwaves move the fleet, overlap between a strong and a weak summer should be lower than between two summers of the same kind.

```{r grp-overlap}
#| code-summary: "Pairwise overlap of trawling between summers"
#| cache: false

fleet_y <- read.csv("outputs/fleet_MHW_cells_year.csv")
yr_class <- distinct(fleet_y, region, year, class)

core_cells <- function(d, share = 0.8) {
  d <- arrange(d, desc(hours))
  d[cumsum(d$hours) / sum(d$hours) <= share | seq_len(nrow(d)) == 1, c("Lon", "Lat")]
}
pair_overlap <- function(reg) {
  d <- filter(fleet_y, region == reg)
  yrs <- sort(unique(d$year))
  bind_rows(lapply(combn(yrs, 2, simplify = FALSE), \(p) {
    a <- filter(d, year == p[1]); b <- filter(d, year == p[2])
    m <- full_join(a |> transmute(Lon, Lat, pa = hours / sum(hours)),
                   b |> transmute(Lon, Lat, pb = hours / sum(hours)), by = c("Lon", "Lat")) |>
      mutate(across(c(pa, pb), \(x) coalesce(x, 0)))
    ca <- core_cells(a); cb <- core_cells(b)
    tibble(region = reg, y1 = p[1], y2 = p[2],
           D = 1 - 0.5 * sum(abs(m$pa - m$pb)),
           jaccard = nrow(inner_join(ca, cb, by = c("Lon", "Lat"))) /
             nrow(distinct(bind_rows(ca, cb))))
  }))
}
overlap_g <- bind_rows(lapply(unique(fleet_y$region), pair_overlap)) |>
  left_join(yr_class |> rename(y1 = year, c1 = class), by = c("region", "y1")) |>
  left_join(yr_class |> rename(y2 = year, c2 = class), by = c("region", "y2")) |>
  mutate(pair = case_when(c1 == c2 & c1 == "strong" ~ "Strong vs strong",
                          c1 == c2 ~ "Weak vs weak", TRUE ~ "Strong vs weak"))

# Centre of gravity per summer and its distance to the area's six-summer centre
cog_g <- fleet_y |>
  group_by(region, year, class) |>
  summarise(lon = weighted.mean(Lon, hours), lat = weighted.mean(Lat, hours), .groups = "drop") |>
  group_by(region) |>
  mutate(shift_km = sqrt(((lon - mean(lon)) * 111.32 * cos(mean(lat) * pi / 180))^2 + ((lat - mean(lat)) * 110.57)^2)) |>
  ungroup()
```

```{r fig-grp-overlap}
#| cache: false
#| fig-cap: "Overlap of trawling between every pair of summers, by area. Left: Schoener's D between effort distributions on the 0.05° grid (1 = identical). Right: Jaccard overlap of core grounds (cells holding 80% of each summer's hours). Bold years are strong heatwave summers. Pairs of a strong and a weak summer are outlined in black."
#| fig-width: 11
#| fig-height: 5.6

ov_long <- bind_rows(overlap_g, overlap_g |> rename(y1 = y2, y2 = y1, c1 = c2, c2 = c1)) |>
  pivot_longer(c(D, jaccard), names_to = "measure") |>
  mutate(measure = recode(measure, D = "Schoener's D", jaccard = "Core grounds (Jaccard)"),
         mixed = pair == "Strong vs weak")
ov_plot <- function(reg) {
  d <- filter(ov_long, region == reg)
  strong <- sort(unique(d$y1[d$c1 == "strong"]))
  lv <- c(sort(unique(d$y1[d$c1 == "weak"])), strong)
  d <- mutate(d, y1 = factor(y1, lv), y2 = factor(y2, lv))
  face <- ifelse(lv %in% strong, "bold", "plain")
  ggplot(d, aes(y1, y2, fill = value)) +
    geom_tile(colour = "white", linewidth = 0.6) +
    geom_tile(data = filter(d, mixed), colour = "black", linewidth = 0.4, fill = NA) +
    geom_text(aes(label = sprintf("%.2f", value)), size = 2.8) +
    scale_fill_gradient(low = "white", high = pal_ocean[["surface"]], limits = c(0.4, 1), oob = squish, name = NULL) +
    facet_wrap(~measure) + labs(title = reg, x = NULL, y = NULL) + theme_ocean(9) +
    theme(axis.text.x = element_text(face = face), axis.text.y = element_text(face = face),
          panel.grid = element_blank(), legend.position = "none")
}
ov_plot("GSA 6") / ov_plot("GSAs 17-18")
```

```{r tbl-grp-overlap}
#| cache: false
#| tbl-cap: "Mean overlap of trawling between summers, by type of pair. Area: GSA 6 or GSAs 17-18. Pair: two strong heatwave summers, two weak ones, or one of each. Pairs: number of pairs of summers. Schoener's D: mean overlap of the effort distributions (1 = identical). Core grounds (Jaccard): mean overlap of the cells holding 80% of each summer's hours. Centre-of-gravity shift (km), given in the strong vs weak row: distance between the mean centre of gravity of the strong summers and that of the weak summers."
#| classes: tbl-compact

cog_shift <- cog_g |>
  group_by(region, class) |> summarise(lon = mean(lon), lat = mean(lat), .groups = "drop") |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = class, values_from = c(lon, lat)) |>
  mutate(shift = sqrt(((lon_strong - lon_weak) * 111.32 * cos(lat_weak * pi / 180))^2 +
                        ((lat_strong - lat_weak) * 110.57)^2))
overlap_tab <- overlap_g |>
  group_by(Area = region, Pair = pair) |>
  summarise(Pairs = n(), `Schoener's D` = round(mean(D), 2),
            `Core grounds (Jaccard)` = round(mean(jaccard), 2), .groups = "drop") |>
  left_join(cog_shift |> transmute(Area = region, Pair = "Strong vs weak", `Centre-of-gravity shift (km)` = round(shift, 1)),
            by = c("Area", "Pair"))
kable(overlap_tab |> mutate(`Centre-of-gravity shift (km)` = coalesce(as.character(`Centre-of-gravity shift (km)`), "")))
```

#### 2c.11.2 Overlap with red mullet habitat and with the heat

The same yearly effort can be related to the two layers of Section 2c, cell by cell: the red mullet biomass predicted for that summer's year, and that summer's heatwave intensity (nearest prediction cell, for trawling within 5 km of the prediction grid: `r percent(with(filter(fleet_y, region == "GSA 6"), sum(hours[on_grid]) / sum(hours)), 1)` of the hours in GSA 6, where much trawling is deeper than the grid, and `r percent(with(filter(fleet_y, region == "GSAs 17-18"), sum(hours[on_grid]) / sum(hours)), 1)` in the Adriatic).

```{r tbl-grp-habitat-overlap}
#| cache: false
#| tbl-cap: "Overlap of trawling with red mullet and with heatwaves, by area and type of summer (mean of three summers; trawling within 5 km of the prediction grid). Area: GSA 6 or GSAs 17-18. Summer: strong or weak heatwave summer. Effort in red mullet hotspots: share of trawling hours in the cells with the highest predicted red mullet biomass that year (top 25% of grid cells). Heatwave exposure ratio: mean heatwave intensity of the strong summers (cumulative, per cell) weighted by each summer's trawling hours, divided by its mean over all grid cells (above 1: trawling sits in the cells that get hotter in heatwave summers; below 1: in the cooler cells). The same heat map is used for both types of summer, so a lower ratio in strong summers than in weak ones would mean the fleet moves away from the heat."
#| classes: tbl-compact

# Heat map of the strong summers: mean cumulative intensity per 0.05° cell over the strong years
strong_heat <- mhw_g |>
  semi_join(yr_class |> filter(class == "strong"), by = c("region", YEAR = "year")) |>
  mutate(Lon = floor(X / 0.05) * 0.05 + 0.025, Lat = floor(Y / 0.05) * 0.05 + 0.025) |>
  group_by(region, Lon, Lat) |> summarise(heat = mean(mhw_cum_intensity, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") |>
  filter(is.finite(heat)) |>
  group_by(region) |> mutate(heat_area = mean(heat)) |> ungroup()

hab_g <- fleet_y |>
  filter(on_grid) |>
  left_join(bind_rows(readRDS("data/group/pred_6.rds") |> mutate(region = "GSA 6"),
                      readRDS("data/group/pred_1718.rds") |> mutate(region = "GSAs 17-18")) |>
              group_by(region, year) |> summarise(q75 = quantile(dens, 0.75), .groups = "drop"),
            by = c("region", "year")) |>
  mutate(Lon = round(Lon, 3), Lat = round(Lat, 3)) |>
  left_join(strong_heat |> mutate(Lon = round(Lon, 3), Lat = round(Lat, 3)), by = c("region", "Lon", "Lat")) |>
  group_by(region, year, class) |>
  summarise(hot_share = sum(hours[dens >= q75]) / sum(hours),
            mhw_ratio = sum((heat * hours)[!is.na(heat)]) / sum(hours[!is.na(heat)]) / first(na.omit(heat_area)),
            .groups = "drop")
kable(hab_g |>
        group_by(Area = region, Summer = recode(class, strong = "Strong MHW", weak = "Weak MHW")) |>
        summarise(`Effort in red mullet hotspots` = percent(mean(hot_share), 1),
                  `Heatwave exposure ratio` = sprintf("%.2f", mean(mhw_ratio)),
                  .groups = "drop"))
```

```{r fig-grp-core}
#| cache: false
#| fig-cap: "Core trawling grounds (cells holding 80% of the mean summer hours) in strong and weak heatwave summers, on the 0.05° grid. Blue-grey: core in both; red: core only in strong heatwave summers; dark blue: core only in weak ones."
#| fig-width: 11
#| fig-height: 5.2

core_class <- fleet_y |>
  group_by(region, class, Lon, Lat) |> summarise(hours = sum(hours) / 3, .groups = "drop") |>
  group_by(region, class) |> group_modify(~ core_cells(.x) |> mutate(core = TRUE)) |> ungroup() |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = class, values_from = core, values_fill = FALSE) |>
  mutate(status = case_when(strong & weak ~ "Core in both", strong ~ "Strong summers only", TRUE ~ "Weak summers only"),
         status = factor(status, c("Core in both", "Strong summers only", "Weak summers only")))
core_cols <- c(`Core in both` = "#9fb7c9", `Strong summers only` = pal_ocean[["alert"]], `Weak summers only` = pal_ocean[["deep"]])
core_map <- function(reg, view) {
  ggplot() + geom_tile(data = filter(core_class, region == reg), aes(Lon, Lat, fill = status), width = 0.05, height = 0.05) +
    land + scale_fill_manual(values = core_cols, name = NULL, drop = FALSE) + view + labs(title = reg) + theme_map
}
(core_map("GSA 6", gsa6_view) | core_map("GSAs 17-18", adr_view)) +
  plot_layout(guides = "collect") & theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```

```{r grp-overlap-nums}
#| include: false
#| cache: false
ovn <- function(reg, pr, col) overlap_tab[[col]][overlap_tab$Area == reg & overlap_tab$Pair == pr]
core_share <- core_class |> group_by(region) |> summarise(both = mean(status == "Core in both"))
hab_m <- hab_g |> group_by(region, class) |> summarise(hot = mean(hot_share), ratio = mean(mhw_ratio), .groups = "drop")
hab_txt <- function(reg) with(filter(hab_m, region == reg), sprintf("%s against %s", percent(hot[class == "strong"], 1), percent(hot[class == "weak"], 1)))
exp_txt <- function(reg) with(filter(hab_m, region == reg), sprintf("%.2f against %.2f", ratio[class == "strong"], ratio[class == "weak"]))
```

The fleets fish the same grounds in strong and weak heatwave summers. In GSA 6, the overlap between a strong and a weak summer (D = `r ovn("GSA 6", "Strong vs weak", "Schoener's D")`) is as high as between two summers of the same kind (`r ovn("GSA 6", "Strong vs strong", "Schoener's D")` and `r ovn("GSA 6", "Weak vs weak", "Schoener's D")`), and the same holds in the Adriatic (`r ovn("GSAs 17-18", "Strong vs weak", "Schoener's D")` against `r ovn("GSAs 17-18", "Strong vs strong", "Schoener's D")` and `r ovn("GSAs 17-18", "Weak vs weak", "Schoener's D")`). The centre of gravity of trawling moves by `r ovn("GSA 6", "Strong vs weak", "Centre-of-gravity shift (km)")` km in GSA 6 and `r ovn("GSAs 17-18", "Strong vs weak", "Centre-of-gravity shift (km)")` km in the Adriatic between the two types of summer, and `r percent(core_share$both[1], 1)` and `r percent(core_share$both[2], 1)` of core cells are core in both. The cells that are core in only one type of summer are scattered along the edges of the main grounds, as expected from year-to-year variation. The share of effort on red mullet hotspots barely changes (`r hab_txt('GSA 6')` in GSA 6, `r hab_txt('GSAs 17-18')` in the Adriatic, strong against weak summers). Relative to where heatwaves strike, the fleet is not displaced either: the heatwave exposure ratio is `r exp_txt('GSA 6')` in GSA 6 and `r exp_txt('GSAs 17-18')` in the Adriatic (strong against weak summers). Ratios close to 1 in both types of summer mean that trawling is spread across hot and cool cells in proportion to the grid, and does not shift away from the cells that heat up most.

> **Discussion points.** (1) With three summers per group, year-to-year differences that have nothing to do with heatwaves (fuel prices, closures, COVID-19 in 2020, a strong heatwave summer in GSA 6 and a weak one in the Adriatic) weigh as much as the heatwave contrast. (2) Summer-level metrics may hide short-term responses: heatwaves last days to weeks. A stronger design uses the daily data already downloaded, comparing effort on heatwave days and on other days of the same summers in the same cells. (3) Across all summers from 2015 to 2021, a regression of each fleet metric on the area's heatwave intensity would use all years instead of six. (4) Management measures that changed over the period, such as spatial closures, should be checked before reading local patches in the map as heatwave responses.

## 3. Marine heatwaves and fleet behaviour

### 3.1 Detecting marine heatwaves

Marine heatwaves (MHWs) are periods of at least five consecutive days during which SST exceeds the seasonally varying 90th percentile of a baseline climatology (Hobday et al. 2016). They are detected with `heatwaveR` on daily L4 SST (Copernicus SST_MED_SST_L4_REP_OBSERVATIONS_010_021), extracted at each prediction grid point in GSA 6. Only events peaking in June-August are kept, when thermal stress is highest in the Mediterranean.

```{r step3-mhw}
#| eval: false
#| code-summary: "Detect MHWs at each grid point (not evaluated: daily SST NetCDF)"

library(terra); library(sf); library(heatwaveR); library(lubridate)

sst  <- rast("data/raw/sst_MED_daily_2010_2021.nc") - 273.15
gsa6 <- st_read("data/raw/GSAs/GSAs_simplified.shp") |>
  filter(SMU_CODE == 6) |> vect()
sst6 <- mask(crop(sst, gsa6), gsa6)

pts <- read.csv("data/raw/MED.env_grid_hindcast_2012_2021.csv") |>
  filter(GSA == 6, MONTH == 7) |> distinct(grid.id, grid.X, grid.Y)
pts.v <- vect(pts, geom = c("grid.X", "grid.Y"), crs = "EPSG:4326")

sst6.long <- as.data.frame(terra::extract(sst6, pts.v)[, -1]) |>
  setNames(as.character(as.Date(time(sst6)))) |>
  mutate(grid.id = pts.v$grid.id) |>
  pivot_longer(-grid.id, names_to = "date", values_to = "sst") |>
  mutate(date = as.Date(date)) |>
  group_by(grid.id) |> filter(!all(is.na(sst))) |> ungroup()

mhw.events <- sst6.long |>
  group_by(grid.id) |>
  group_modify(~ {
    clim <- ts2clm(.x, x = date, y = sst,
                   climatologyPeriod = c("2010-01-01", "2021-12-31"))
    ev <- detect_event(clim, x = date, y = sst)$event
    if (nrow(ev) == 0) data.frame() else ev
  }) |>
  filter(month(date_peak) %in% 6:8)

mhw.year <- expand.grid(grid.id = unique(pts$grid.id), YEAR = 2012:2021) |>
  left_join(pts, by = "grid.id") |>
  left_join(mhw.events |>
              mutate(YEAR = year(date_peak)) |>
              group_by(grid.id, YEAR) |>
              summarise(mhw_frequency = n(), mhw_days = sum(duration),
                        mhw_mean_duration = mean(duration),
                        mhw_mean_intensity = mean(intensity_mean),
                        mhw_max_intensity = max(intensity_max),
                        mhw_cum_intensity = sum(intensity_cumulative),
                        .groups = "drop"),
            by = c("grid.id", "YEAR")) |>
  mutate(across(starts_with("mhw_"), \(x) replace_na(x, 0)))
write.table(mhw.year, "outputs/MHW_gsa6.csv", sep = ";", row.names = FALSE)
```

```{r tbl-mhw}
#| tbl-cap: "Summer marine heatwave (MHW) metrics by year, averaged over the GSA 6 grid points (events peaking in June-August). Year. Events: mean number of MHW events per grid point. MHW days: mean number of days under MHW conditions. Mean intensity (°C): mean SST anomaly during events, relative to the seasonal climatology. Cumulative intensity (°C days): sum of the daily anomalies over all events. Used as: role of the year in the fleet comparison (MHW, non-MHW or not used)."
#| code-summary: "Load annual MHW metrics and summarise across GSA 6"
#| classes: tbl-compact

mhw.year <- read.csv("outputs/MHW_gsa6.csv", sep = ";")

years.MHW   <- c(2017, 2018, 2020)
years.noMHW <- c(2013, 2014, 2016)

mhw.gsa <- mhw.year |>
  group_by(YEAR) |>
  summarise(across(starts_with("mhw_"), mean), .groups = "drop") |>
  mutate(group = case_when(YEAR %in% years.MHW ~ "MHW",
                           YEAR %in% years.noMHW ~ "non-MHW",
                           TRUE ~ "not used"))

kable(mhw.gsa |>
        transmute(Year = YEAR, Events = round(mhw_frequency, 2),
                  `MHW days` = round(mhw_days, 1),
                  `Mean intensity (°C)` = round(mhw_mean_intensity, 2),
                  `Cumulative intensity (°C days)` = round(mhw_cum_intensity, 1),
                  `Used as` = group))
```

```{r fig-mhw-years}
#| fig-cap: "Mean summer cumulative MHW intensity across GSA 6 grid cells, coloured by how each year is used in the fleet comparison."
#| fig-width: 8
#| fig-height: 3.8

ggplot(mhw.gsa, aes(YEAR, mhw_cum_intensity, fill = group)) +
  geom_col() +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("MHW" = pal_ocean[["alert"]],
                               "non-MHW" = pal_ocean[["surface"]],
                               "not used" = pal_ocean[["grey"]]), name = NULL) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = 2012:2021) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Cumulative intensity (°C days)") + theme_ocean()
```

```{r fig-mhw-map}
#| fig-cap: "Summer cumulative MHW intensity per grid cell, 2012-2021."
#| fig-width: 11
#| fig-height: 6

ggplot(mhw.year) + land +
  geom_point(aes(grid.X, grid.Y, colour = mhw_cum_intensity), size = 0.45) +
  scale_colour_viridis_c(option = "inferno", name = "Cumulative intensity (°C days)") +
  gsa6_view + facet_wrap(~YEAR, ncol = 5) + theme_map
```

Cumulative intensity combines duration and magnitude into a single measure of thermal stress. Summers 2017, 2018 and 2020 stand out, with 2015 also strong. 2014 and 2016 had no summer events.

> **Discussion point: baseline length.** The climatology is built on 2010-2021, against the 30-year baseline recommended by Hobday et al. (2016). A short, recent baseline that already contains the warming trend raises the threshold and under-detects events.

### 3.2 Trawling in heatwave and non-heatwave summers

Daily trawler effort at 0.01° is pulled for June-August of the six selected years, clipped to the GSA 6 polygon. Each cell is given a depth (NOAA ETOPO via `marmap`) and a distance to the nearest coastline (Natural Earth), and fleet indicators are compared between the two groups of years.

```{r step3-fleet}
#| eval: false
#| code-summary: "Pull daily summer effort and derive fleet indicators (not evaluated: GFW API)"

library(gfwr); library(marmap); library(rnaturalearth)
key <- gfw_auth()

daily_fishing_hrs <- purrr::map_dfr(c(years.MHW, years.noMHW), function(yr) {
  gfw_ais_fishing_hours(
    spatial_resolution = "HIGH", temporal_resolution = "DAILY",
    start_date = paste0(yr, "-06-01"), end_date = paste0(yr, "-09-01"),
    region_source = "USER_SHAPEFILE", region = st_as_sf(gsa6), key = key)
})

trawlers_gridded_hrs <- daily_fishing_hrs |>
  mutate(year = year(`Time Range`),
         mhw = if_else(year %in% years.MHW, "mhw", "no_mhw")) |>
  filter(`Gear Type` == "TRAWLERS")

bathy_grid <- getNOAA.bathy(
  lon1 = min(trawlers_gridded_hrs$Lon) - 1, lon2 = max(trawlers_gridded_hrs$Lon) + 1,
  lat1 = min(trawlers_gridded_hrs$Lat) - 1, lat2 = max(trawlers_gridded_hrs$Lat) + 1,
  resolution = 1, keep = TRUE)
trawlers_gridded_hrs$depth <- get.depth(bathy_grid,
  x = trawlers_gridded_hrs[, c("Lon", "Lat")], locator = FALSE)$depth

unique_coords <- distinct(trawlers_gridded_hrs, Lon, Lat)
unique_sf <- st_as_sf(unique_coords, coords = c("Lon", "Lat"), crs = 4326)
coastline <- ne_coastline(scale = "large", returnclass = "sf") |>
  st_crop(st_bbox(unique_sf) + c(-2, -2, 2, 2))
unique_coords$dist_to_coast_km <-
  as.numeric(apply(st_distance(unique_sf, coastline), 1, min)) / 1000
trawlers_gridded_hrs <- left_join(trawlers_gridded_hrs, unique_coords, by = c("Lon", "Lat"))

fishing.maps <- trawlers_gridded_hrs |>
  group_by(Lon, Lat, year, mhw) |>
  summarise(annual_fishing_hours = sum(`Apparent Fishing Hours`, na.rm = TRUE),
            .groups = "drop") |>
  summarise(mean_fishing_hours = mean(annual_fishing_hours), .by = c(Lon, Lat, mhw))

fishing.change <- fishing.maps |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = mhw, values_from = mean_fishing_hours) |>
  drop_na(mhw, no_mhw) |>
  mutate(difference = mhw - no_mhw, log_ratio = log((mhw + 1) / (no_mhw + 1)))

write.csv(fishing.maps, "outputs/fishing_maps_MHW.csv", row.names = FALSE)
write.csv(fishing.change, "outputs/fishing_change_MHW.csv", row.names = FALSE)
```

```{r fig-fleet-png}
#| fig-cap: "Group output: mean summer trawler effort in non-MHW and MHW years, their difference and log ratio."
#| out-width: "90%"

include_graphics("outputs/Fishing_effort_MHW_comparison.png")
```

```{r tbl-fleet}
#| tbl-cap: "Summer trawler effort in GSA 6 in MHW years (2017, 2018, 2020) and non-MHW years (2013, 2014, 2016), from daily GFW AIS apparent fishing hours on a 0.01° grid. Period: MHW or non-MHW years. Cells fished: number of 0.01° cells with trawler effort in at least one year of the period. Total mean hours: sum over cells of the mean annual summer fishing hours. Median hours per cell: median of the per-cell mean annual summer fishing hours."
#| code-summary: "Summarise the saved spatial comparison"
#| classes: tbl-compact

fishing.change <- read.csv("outputs/fishing_change_MHW.csv")
fishing.maps   <- read.csv("outputs/fishing_maps_MHW.csv")

fleet_tab <- fishing.maps |>
  group_by(Period = if_else(mhw == "mhw", "MHW years", "non-MHW years")) |>
  summarise(`Cells fished` = n(),
            `Total mean hours` = round(sum(mean_fishing_hours)),
            `Median hours per cell` = round(median(mean_fishing_hours), 2),
            .groups = "drop")
kable(fleet_tab)
```

Of the cells fished in at least one period, `r fmt(nrow(fishing.change))` were fished in both and enter the change maps. In `r percent(mean(fishing.change$difference > 0), 1)` of them, effort was higher in heatwave summers.

> **Discussion point: confounding with AIS uptake.** The non-MHW years include 2013 and 2014, when trawler AIS coverage was still growing (Step 1). Higher effort in MHW years is therefore expected even with no change in behaviour. Picking contrasting years from 2015 onward (e.g. 2016 vs 2017), or comparing effort per vessel, would separate the two. Two smaller points: cells missing in a year are not counted as zero in `fishing.maps`, which inflates means, and depth and distance to coast are averaged over cells rather than weighted by fishing hours.

## 4. Climate-fisheries vulnerability index

Vulnerability is classically framed as exposure plus sensitivity minus adaptive capacity. The Climate-Fisheries Vulnerability Index (CFVI) combines three indicators, each rescaled to 0-1 and averaged with equal weights:

- **Exposure**: summer cumulative MHW intensity in 2021.
- **Sensitivity**: percentage change in predicted fish abundance 2012-2021, on the abundance scale (the sign is flipped so that habitat loss raises vulnerability).
- **Pressure**: AIS trawler fishing hours in 2021.

```{r step4-cfvi}
#| dependson: ["fig-pred", "step2-change"]
#| code-summary: "Build the index from the saved outputs"

norm <- function(x) { rng <- range(x, na.rm = TRUE); (x - rng[1]) / (rng[2] - rng[1]) }

cfvi <- mhw.year |>
  filter(YEAR == 2021) |>
  select(grid.id, grid.X, grid.Y, mhw_cum_intensity) |>
  left_join(select(fish.change6, grid.id, perc.change), by = "grid.id") |>  # back-transformed change
  left_join(fish.pred6 |> filter(year == 2021) |>
              select(grid.id, fishing_pressure = fishing_hours), by = "grid.id") |>
  mutate(exposure    = norm(mhw_cum_intensity),
         pressure    = norm(fishing_pressure),
         sensitivity = norm(-perc.change),
         CFVI = (exposure + pressure + sensitivity) / 3)

# write.csv(cfvi, "outputs/CFVI_GSA6.csv", row.names = FALSE)  # group output, left untouched
```

```{r fig-cfvi}
#| dependson: "step4-cfvi"
#| fig-cap: "The three CFVI components and the combined index for GSA 6."
#| fig-width: 11
#| fig-height: 9

cfvi_long <- cfvi |>
  select(grid.X, grid.Y, Exposure = exposure, Sensitivity = sensitivity,
         Pressure = pressure, CFVI) |>
  pivot_longer(-c(grid.X, grid.Y)) |>
  mutate(name = factor(name, c("Exposure", "Sensitivity", "Pressure", "CFVI")))

ggplot(cfvi_long) + land +
  geom_point(aes(grid.X, grid.Y, colour = value), size = 0.9) +
  scale_colour_gradientn(colours = c("darkgreen", "green", "yellow", "orange", "red", "darkred"),
                         na.value = "grey60", name = "Score (0-1)") +
  gsa6_view + facet_wrap(~name, ncol = 2) + theme_map
```

```{r tbl-cfvi}
#| tbl-cap: "Distribution of the climate-fisheries vulnerability index (CFVI) components across GSA 6 grid cells. component: exposure (2021 cumulative MHW intensity), sensitivity (decline in predicted total fish abundance, 2012-2021), pressure (2021 trawler fishing hours) and CFVI (the mean of the three), each min-max scaled to 0-1. median: median score across cells. share zero: share of cells scoring exactly 0."
#| dependson: "step4-cfvi"
#| code-summary: "Distribution of the index components"
#| classes: tbl-compact

cfvi_sum <- cfvi |>
  summarise(across(c(exposure, sensitivity, pressure, CFVI),
                   list(median = \(x) median(x, na.rm = TRUE),
                        `share zero` = \(x) mean(x == 0, na.rm = TRUE)))) |>
  pivot_longer(everything(), names_to = c("component", ".value"), names_sep = "_")
kable(cfvi_sum |> mutate(median = round(median, 2), `share zero` = percent(`share zero`, 1)))
```

The highest index values sit off the northern Catalan coast (Cap de Creus to Roses) and in nearshore cells off the Ebro delta and Valencia, where moderate heatwave exposure overlaps with heavy trawling and predicted abundance loss.

> **Discussion point: time windows and scaling.** Exposure uses a single, mild heatwave year: `r percent(mean(cfvi$exposure == 0, na.rm = TRUE), 1)` of cells score exactly 0, so the index is mostly driven by pressure and sensitivity in the rest of GSA 6. Pressure is very skewed and min-max scaling squashes most cells near 0. Sensitivity includes the extrapolated coastal cells of Step 2. More defensible choices: mean exposure over 2015-2021, log-transformed effort, habitat change from within the sampled range only, and a check of how the hotspots move under different weights.

## Summary and next steps

The pipeline links survey, environmental, heatwave and AIS data into a coherent spatial workflow. Before interpreting the results, four points are worth addressing as a group:

1. **AIS ramp-up**: start comparisons in 2015, or normalise effort per vessel, so that changes in AIS coverage are not read as changes in fishing.
2. **Extrapolation**: predict in the survey months (May-June) and within the sampled depth range, so that habitat change and the sensitivity score are not driven by out-of-range coastal cells.
3. **Zeros**: treat unmatched hauls and unfished cells consistently as zero effort in fitting, prediction and averaging.
4. **Index design**: align the time windows of the three CFVI components and test sensitivity to transformation and weights.

For **red mullet**, the group's spatio-temporal model (Section 2c) extends the analysis to the Adriatic and gives a broadly stable GSA 6 biomass index from 2015 to 2021; like the Tweedie GAM of Section 2b, it shows no increase. In Section 2b, the model with zeros, a Tweedie family and depth explains about half the deviance and predicts a widespread decline in June density from 2015 to 2021 that holds when fishing effort is held constant. Natural next steps are to identify which environmental term drives the decline, check it against the observed MEDITS trend, and feed the red mullet habitat change into the vulnerability index in place of total fish abundance.

Smaller fixes (grid alignment in the haul join, MHW baseline length, weighted depth and distance means, the unfinished daily block in Script 1) are listed in `review_notes.md`.
